core.title: Keep the journey view generated from the current plan
core.given: The repository documents itself (its documentation tree exists) and its plan declares at least one journey or interlocking.
core.when: You finish any plan work or review in that repository, whether or not you touched the plan or the generated view; pre-existing drift and generator upgrades count.
core.then: The generated journey view must contain exactly, byte-for-byte, what the stack's generator renders from the current plan: the view's index page plus one diagram per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed train.
prefer: Regenerate and commit the view with the stack's generation command.
Fix what the view shows in the plan, then regenerate.
If the view's index page is hand-written, move its content elsewhere first.
Keep the gaps table (unreached interlockings, open routes, unrouted trains) visible and accurately rendered; it is part of the contract.
avoid: Hand-editing or adding files in the generated view; change the plan, never the generated files.
Leaving the view missing or stale, or keeping files the generator does not produce.
Skipping the page when the plan has interlockings but no journey; it shows every interlocking as unreached.
Treating the view as acceptance evidence; it renders planned behaviour only.
unless: The repository does not document itself (no documentation tree).
The plan declares no journey and no interlocking.
core.why: A hand-drawn journey page drifts from the plan the moment either changes; generating it and failing on any difference keeps documented journeys equal to planned ones and lets reviewers judge a decomposition without reading the plan's raw interlocking declarations.
evidence: Running the stack's generation command against the current plan produces no diff in the generated view (no missing, changed or extra files).

The committed view shows, top down: each journey map (entry action, interlockings, chosen routes, trains run, continuations and terminal outcomes); each journey's nominal path end to end as one sequence across its interlockings; every path as a table; each interlocking's routes with their guards; each train as a sequence diagram; and a table of what the plan leaves unconnected.
For a plan with interlockings but no journey, the page exists and lists every interlocking as unreached, which is the truthful state of the decomposition.
The view answers who hands what to whom, which guard selects which route, and where each path ends.
verification: State-based invariant: a validator compares the committed view files with a fresh render of the current plan produced by the installed generator, and reports any mismatch whether or not the current change touched the plan or the view (pre-existing drift, generator upgrade).

Comparison is byte-for-byte between the committed view files and that fresh render; a missing, stale, hand-edited or extra file in the view is each a violation. Whether the render embeds fields that vary between runs, and whether any normalisation is applied, is a property of the stack's generator, not of this core.

Expected file set: the view's index page plus one diagram per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed train; the index-page file name and the diagram format are supplied by the profile.

Scope gates are repository-state checks: skip when the documentation tree does not exist, or when the plan declares no journey and no interlocking; the second gate requires parsing plan content for actual declarations, which a plan path match alone cannot establish. A plan with interlockings but no journey is in scope.

Diff-level hints (a plan journey/interlocking/route/train added, modified or removed; a view file edited, added or removed; the installed generator's version changed) make a mismatch likely but are not required for the check to fire.

Term 'the view': the generated page, top down: each journey as a map (entry action, interlockings, the routes they choose, the trains they run, continuations and terminal outcomes); the journey's nominal path walked end to end as one sequence across its interlockings; every path as a table; each interlocking's routes with their guards; each train as a sequence diagram; and a table of what the plan leaves unconnected.
Term 'generated': byte-for-byte what the installed generator renders from the current plan.

values: documentation tree present (the repository documents itself)
generated journey view files (index page and diagrams)
journey view missing, stale, hand-edited or extra file
plan journey/interlocking/route/train added, modified or removed
journey view file edited, added or removed

fires: In a repository that documents itself and whose plan declares journeys or interlockings, a planner adds, renames or rewires a journey, interlocking, route or train in the plan and does not regenerate the journey view.
In such a repository, someone edits the view's index page or one of its diagrams by hand.
In a repository whose plan declares interlockings but no journey, no journey page is committed.
In such a repository, the view contains a file the generator would not produce (e.g. a diagram for a removed train).
In such a repository, the committed view was already stale or missing before the current task, even though the task touched neither the plan nor the view.
In such a repository, an upgrade of the installed generator changes the rendered output and the committed view is not regenerated.
doesNotFire: The repository has no documentation tree.
The plan declares no journey and no interlocking.
A plan edit leaves the rendered output byte-identical AND the committed view already matched the generator output (an unchanged render never excuses existing missing, stale or extra files).

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of the repository's self-documentation tree; its existence is scope gate 1 and the no-documentation exception.
Directory of the generated journey view (index page and diagrams) that must match the generator output exactly.
File name of the generated journey view's index page inside the view directory; the generator owns it, and a hand-written one must be moved aside before regenerating.
Format of the generated diagrams the view contains (one per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed train).
The command that regenerates the journey view from the current plan.
Root of the plan artifacts the view is generated from and parsed for journey/interlocking declarations.

proposedKeys.meaning: Root of the repository's self-documentation tree, whose existence puts a repository in scope for documentation rules.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roots group covers config, source, test, e2e, plan, scan and excluded trees, but no documentation root.

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory of the generated journey view (its index page and diagrams) inside the repository, which documentation rules require to match the generator output.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Layout keys place code, plan items, unit/acceptance tests and e2e tests, but not generated documentation views.

proposedKeys.meaning: File name of the generated journey view's index page inside the journey-view directory; the generator owns it.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Layout keys name directories and placement patterns (wagon, feature, plan item, test locations) but never a concrete owned file inside a generated view, and suffix describes file-kind suffixes, not a single generator-owned output file name.

proposedKeys.meaning: Artifact format of the generated diagrams the journey view contains (one per journey map, per journey's nominal path, per routed train).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix's closed file_kind parameter (source, unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test, markup, plan_artifact, config) does not include generated diagram output, and idiom.markup_kinds covers declarative-request markup kinds, not generator output formats.

proposedKeys.meaning: The helper command that regenerates generated documentation views from the current plan.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: enforcement.runner names the convention-check runner, not a generation command, and tooling has no documentation-generation key.

bunOnly.text: (the generator refuses to overwrite it without --force)
bunOnly.reason: The ATDD-Bun generator's overwrite guard and --force flag; other stacks' generators behave differently, and the neutral obligation is carried by the core's advice to move hand-written index content elsewhere first.

bunOnly.text: Rendered output carries no timestamp and no package version, so it changes only when the plan or the renderer changes; no normalisation of such fields is needed.
bunOnly.reason: A determinism property of the ATDD-Bun renderer's output, not a stack-neutral requirement; the core keeps only the neutral byte-for-byte equality with a fresh render, and a stack whose generator embeds varying fields addresses normalisation in its own realization.

bunOnly.text: Generator refuses to overwrite a hand-written docs/purpose/journeys/index.adoc unless run with --force.
bunOnly.reason: Generator-specific overwrite guard and flag; the view directory and index-page file name it names are bound by the profile (layout.journey_view_dir, layout.journey_view.index_page), and the guard itself adds nothing to the neutral obligation beyond prefer[2].
Validator/finding identifier of this rule's ATDD-Bun realization; the core names the check generically.

neutralityNotes: Journey, interlocking, route, guard and train are plan-domain terms (journey already appears in the closed urn vocabulary) and are treated as stack-neutral. Two things could not be made neutral and are kept in bunOnly: (1) the ATDD-Bun renderer's determinism (output carries no timestamp and no package version, hence no normalisation is needed) is a realization property, so the core requires only byte-for-byte equality with a fresh render and a stack whose generator embeds varying fields must address comparison in its own realization; (2) the generator's refusal to overwrite a hand-written index without --force is realization-specific, with only the safe-handling advice (move hand-written content first) kept neutral. The concrete shape of the view's output — the index-page file name and the diagram format — is profile data (proposed layout keys), as are the documentation root, the view directory and the generation command (three further proposed keys: the vocabulary's roots and layout groups cover only source/test/e2e/plan placement, and tooling has no documentation-generation command).
